direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires an ESM-only Node.js port under /output, local .mjs modules, manual argv parsing, pure JS behavior, and no node:crypto interface.
Aggregate parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, four subagents, completed evaluation, 38 of 61 tests passed, and solution_passed false.
Current completed parallel status records artifact files, protocol validation with four child threads, and official evaluation failure at 38/61.
Parallel official evaluator completed successfully as a process but marked the solution failed with 38 passed samples out of 61.
Parallel final answer claims a pure local ESM implementation, lists the final files, and reports sample plus CLI parity checks.

timeline_reviews.summary: Parallel transport timeline mirrors the parent turn, including implementation, reconciliation, duplicate tree cleanup, final checks, and final response.
Parallel parent probes executable behavior, spawns children, creates an initial /output tree, verifies it, observes a child rewrite, removes forbidden imports and duplicate files, then finalizes.
The /root/cli_probe child independently probes CLI behavior and writes a competing /output implementation including /output/test2.mjs and modules that initially import node:crypto and node:path.
The /root/algo_probe child probes PBKDF2 behavior, spawns its own CLI child, writes a separate implementation under /workspace/output, verifies samples, and returns a final answer.
The nested CLI probe supplies argparse observations to algo_probe and does not write final deliverable files itself.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and defines the same ESM, /output, manual CLI, and pure-JS PBKDF2 requirements.
Aggregate serial cell metadata reports no parallel use, no subagents, completed evaluation, 41 of 61 tests passed, and solution_passed false.
Current completed serial status records the final artifact files, disabled multi-agent protocol, and official evaluation failure at 41/61.
Serial official evaluator completed successfully as a process but marked the solution failed with 41 passed samples out of 61.
Serial final answer lists one local ESM module tree and reports sample, help, and parser error verification.

timeline_reviews.summary: Serial transport timeline shows one parent turn with local probing, one implementation patch, verification, and final response without child activity.
Serial actor probes executable behavior, confirms PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 and UTF-8 handling, writes the /output tree once, verifies samples and selected parser cases, and finalizes.

parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs output in /output, manual argparse-like CLI behavior, pure-JS PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, local imports only, and prohibition on node:crypto in submitted code.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent retained implementation ownership while also spawning CLI and algorithm probes; children independently performed overlapping implementation and verification rather than only reporting findings.
parallel.implementation: Parent first wrote encoding, SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, CLI, and test2.mjs modules, then later adopted and repaired a child layout with cli and crypto subdirectories after the child rewrite.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration required cleanup of old parent modules, removal of child node:crypto and node:path imports, creation of a missing sha1 module, and deletion of a duplicate /workspace/output implementation tree.
parallel.verification: Parallel verified the four supplied samples, help and error cases, duplicate flags, UTF-8 behavior, and post-reconciliation checks, but these checks did not cover all hidden official cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 38/61, and the visible trajectory shows process churn from concurrent deliverable rewrites even though the final response claimed the local ESM tree was ready.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs output, local module split, manual CLI parser, UTF-8 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior, and no node:crypto in the final files.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the full path from black-box probing through module creation, verification, and final response, with no delegated writers or shared workspace merge.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote parser, UTF-8 encoding, SHA-1, HMAC-SHA1, PBKDF2, hex formatting, and test2.mjs modules in one apply_patch operation under /output.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The delivered file tree remained a single coherent /output layout; there was no competing /workspace/output tree and no parent-child reconciliation step.
serial.verification: Serial verified all four supplied samples, selected stdout/stderr and argparse cases, negative iteration behavior, final file layout, and node --check on test2.mjs.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 41/61, and visible checks show ordinary emulation gaps such as a raw JavaScript error stack for negative iterations rather than a fully Python-shaped exception.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the core requirements and explicitly removed node:crypto and node:path after a child introduced them.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and wrote only local ESM modules in its final tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the difference is that parallel had to repair a child-created requirement violation while serial never introduced it into the final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across parent, CLI child, algorithm child, and nested CLI probe, but implementation ownership overlapped across actors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for probing, implementation, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained simultaneous probes but created overlapping final-code ownership; serial was slower in parallelism but simpler in ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children had the task prompt context, but no effective file ownership boundary prevented competing /output and /workspace/output layouts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent context boundary; the same actor maintained the parser, crypto, and entrypoint interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface difference is shared-state ownership rather than missing task context: parallel allowed independently produced layouts to claim the same deliverable role.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel moved from an initial flat lib implementation to a reconciled child-style cli/crypto layout after removing built-in imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one cli/encoding/crypto/format module layout in a single local patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's final implementation path was a merge-and-repair path; serial's was a single construction path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited on children, received algo_probe's final answer, interrupted remaining children, and then used workspace inspection to reconcile results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local checks directly informed the next implementation and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lifecycle included waiting and interruption, but the decisive result handling issue was the workspace rewrite, not a trapped completed result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared workspace writes produced a replaced /output/test2.mjs, forbidden built-in imports, and a duplicate /workspace/output tree that the parent removed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and delivered one /output tree without concurrent writers or cleanup of other actors' files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main concrete task-solving difference: parallel had a realized shared-state merge problem while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified samples and several parser cases both before and after cleanup, then reported successful local checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified all four samples, selected parser cases, negative iteration behavior, file layout, and node --check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local smoke tests that missed official hidden failures; parallel repeated checks due to reconciliation, while serial's checks followed its single implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, 147 LLM requests, waits, interrupts, and 509 agent seconds before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout, 28 LLM requests, no subagents, and 271 agent seconds before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget and closure effort on coordination and cleanup, but it still completed before timeout; the budget difference is not itself retained as a load imbalance label.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail: parallel failed at 38/61 and serial failed at 41/61. The concrete process difference is not a pass/fail split but a parallel-only shared-state reconciliation episode: the parent and children produced overlapping deliverables, whereas serial built one coherent tree. The score gap alone does not prove which hidden cases differed.
parallel_contributors: Overlapping child and parent writes replaced the required /output entrypoint and forced cleanup before final delivery.
Parallel final verification was local smoke testing after reconciliation, not comprehensive official coverage.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one implementation owner and avoided merge cleanup.
Serial still missed enough hidden behavior to fail the official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs visibly focused on supplied samples and selected CLI probes, so remaining failures are ordinary black-box emulation gaps not uniquely explained by coordination.
Serial visibly left negative iteration as a raw JavaScript Error stack, while parallel converted that case to a ValueError-style line; neither difference creates an official pass/fail discordance.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel process disadvantage

The parent explicitly performed integration and reconciliation after observing the child rewrite.
The required /output assembly and final response were owned by the parent, even though child writes disrupted them.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition through probing, implementation, cleanup, verification, and final delivery.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and children implemented while probes were still ongoing.
Investigation and implementation overlapped; the adverse event came from concurrent writes, not a separate investigation phase delaying implementation.
The indispensable path was not starved; multiple actors implemented it and the parent completed final delivery before timeout.
Four subagents and high token use are visible, but the run did not exhaust the deadline and the concrete consequence was a write conflict.
No single child was shown to have an overbroad unfinished scope that displaced required work; child outputs were completed or inspected.
Children had the original task prompt context; the wrong /workspace/output placement and forbidden imports are not proven to result from an omitted parent-known brief requirement.
There was missing file ownership in practice, but the realized event was a concrete deliverable overwrite, which the taxonomy says to classify as a write label.
No known finding or constraint is shown to disappear through transfer and cause repeated work; the parent observed and repaired the child file state.
Child handoffs were not shown to be too large to consume; parent decisions were based on direct workspace inspection and targeted cleanup.
No receiver acted on a superseded handoff; the parent reacted to current filesystem contents after the child rewrite.
Although child and parent designs conflicted, the concrete failure was a file rewrite in the shared workspace, not unadjudicated reports at handoff time.
The parent performed visible whole-task checks after reconciliation; official hidden failures alone do not establish an unsupported completion decision.
No replacement child or retry repeated the same work without inherited checkpoints; the observed later work was parent reconciliation.
